note: Edge CPU/RSS + agent->backend wire bytes, measured live on the collapsed single-host stack. Resource numbers are valid independent of the warm sketch READ-path defect (the agent ingests + flushes + ships correctly; the backend stores the sketch state — only the warm sketch QUERY returns empty). CPU% is the docker-stats instantaneous sample taken ~70s after replay (post-flush idle); peak flush CPU is higher but bursty.

compound_all_6_families.dataset: /tmp/gct-aliased.jsonl (800k OTLP points: 100k cpu_rate + 100k memory + 6x100k family aliases)
compound_all_6_families.comment: One collector running sum + ddsketch + kll + hll + countsketch(+heap) + countminsketch simultaneously. 800k raw points aggregate to 5559 sketch/sum envelopes on the wire (143x reduction in point count). 25.7 MB total wire for the compound (delta-transmitted).

countsketch_heap_vs_noheap.dataset: /tmp/gct-aliased.jsonl (full); each arm also carries the two Sum metrics, so wire includes the sum baseline
countsketch_heap_vs_noheap.comment: Heap-bearing CountSketch ships ~14% LESS wire (57.9 vs 67.5 MB) and uses ~29% LESS edge RSS (74.8 vs 105.4 MiB) than the plain matrix-only CountSketch, while ALSO being the only one that can answer topk() warm (FrequencyTopk capability). Plain CountSketch (no heap) ships the full count matrix and CANNOT serve topk warm (capability miss -> archive failover). This is the direction of the recall-aware-topk finding: the bounded heap is the compact, query-answering representation. (The wire totals include the two Sum metrics common to both arms, so the per-family delta is a lower bound on the heap's relative saving.)
